title: gasoline: lighting your creative fuel
content:
artifacts are metaphorical-poetic teachings for navigating the creative life, released as a part of labyrinth library.

you can listen to an excerpt below ~

explore this artifact

it wasn’t until creating this artifact that I understood something about fire — as a chemical process that happens under the right conditions. fire is not a mysterious, divinely-inspired thing. in order to burn, you need 3 ingredients — FUEL, OXYGEN, HEAT. applied to the creative life, this means giving your inspiration the right burning material, space, and initial spark to catch a flame, and sustain it. fire requires feeding, like anything else. fire has needs.

I’ve written about how the work is hard and lonely — therefore, you must be your own flame. what are the conditions for creative flammability? how do you allow ideas, projects, urges, desires — to catch fire? how do you tend to a fire, over time? I find that goals are not enough; your vision is the fuel source — vision is like a magic fire in a jar.

part of the heart work, then, is meeting where we have unconscious resistance to our own fire. in what ways do we fear that our fire could harm the things we cherish? like relating to all the elements, we can learn strategies, tools, and containers to be in active relationship to our fire — as hearth-keeper, flamethrower - in whatever way we need.


*
purpose — working with the ingredients of your creative fire. making the process of preparation itself — a ritual every bit as essential as actually being in the flame. create conditions for creative volatility and flammability.

guiding question — what is the nature of your creative fuel? what can you pour into the material of your process to make it more flammable? what does being creatively reckless look like for you?
